title: A rare charge-separated zwitterionic tri-aluminum complex
content: A non-symmetric N-imidoylamidine–thioether–amine ligand was isolated and found to stabilize a rare charge-separated zwitterionic tri-aluminum complex upon reaction with trimethylaluminum. X-ray diffraction, multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, and DFT analyses reveal a charge-separated framework in which a single ligand supports both electron-rich and electron-deficient aluminum environments. Thermal treatment affords a neutral tetra-aluminum dimer through ligand fragmentation and methyl redistribution, forming an elusive 16-membered macrocyclic structure. This work expands zwitterionic aluminum chemistry beyond monometallic systems and highlights the ability of the present ligand to stabilize electronically distinct aluminum environments.
